newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan raises caps on foreign-held share equity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan raises caps on foreign-held share equity.

text.p: The central bank and finance ministry said on Monday they had agreed to raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stock-market equity to 25 percent from 20 percent.
The two agencies, in a joint announcement, said the ceiling on foreign investment in any single listed company was being raised to 10 percent from 7.5 percent.
The liberalisation would be put into effect by the end of 1996, officials from both agencies said.
The changes were agreed in an afternoon meeting of senior officials of the central bank and finance ministry.
At end-August values, the liberalisation would allow foreign interests to own US$59.6 billion of equity in Taiwan shares, the agencies said in a joint statement.
Under the 20 percent cap, the maximum was US$47.7 billion.
The changes were intended to expand the scale of the stock market and further implement Taiwan's financial liberalisation and internationalisation, it said.
The ceilings originally were conceived to ensure local control of Taiwan equities and stabilise the local financial markets.
The limits are enforced by obliging foreign institutions to obtain permits allowing them to invest in Taiwan shares. Permits are issued periodically and are valid for six months.
